title: Mung-Nificent Breakfast Muffins
subtitle: egg-free veggie egg bites
menu_blurb: Fluffy, protein-packed breakfast bites made from blended split mung beans, baked with sautéed onion, peppers and spinach. No eggs needed.
intro: A great breakfast full of bean protein. Instead of eggs, we use a copycat of “Just Egg,” but much more flavorful and without any of the unhealthy additives. Think Starbucks egg bites without the egg. There are so many ways to use this recipe, and this version makes a great bite-size treat!
origin: Mung beans come from the Indian subcontinent, where they were first domesticated around 4,500 years ago. Archaeologists have found carbonized mung bean seeds linked to the ancient Indus Valley (Harappan) civilization in modern-day India and Pakistan. Split yellow mung beans, known as moong dal, are green mung beans that have been skinned and split in half, exposing the bright yellow inside and changing how they behave in the kitchen.

mise_en_place.label: Gather
mise_en_place.task: Paprikas, onion powder, garlic powder, nutritional yeast, salt, pepper, turmeric, and baking powder

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A muffin tin, a sauté pan, and a blender

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: Spray the muffin tin thoroughly with avocado oil spray.
Chop the onion and peppers, and roughly chop the spinach.

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
instructions: Start with the onion, then layer in the peppers, then the spinach. Cook until soft.

steps.title: Blend
instructions: Blend all of the Mung-nificent blend ingredients until smooth.

steps.title: Fill the tin
instructions: Divide the vegetables among the muffin cups.
Pour the mung bean blend over the top to fill each cup.

steps.title: Bake
instructions: Bake for about 25 to 35 minutes, checking with a toothpick until cooked all the way through.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more spices, or roasted potatoes.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Use different vegetables. Or make a frittata instead: pour the same mixture over the vegetables and roasted potatoes in a baking dish and bake at 400°F for 30 to 40 minutes.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps in the fridge or freezer.

notebook.question: Are mung beans good for you?
answer: Mung beans are an exceptionally nutrient-dense legume, with plant protein, fiber, and essential minerals. Their nutrition numbers look very different dry versus cooked, because the beans absorb a lot of water as they cook.

notebook.question: What is nutritional yeast, and is it good for you?
answer: Nutritional yeast is a deactivated yeast from the same species used to bake bread and brew beer. The yeast cells are inactive, so it won’t make bread rise or ferment anything.
It is exceptionally good for you, with plant protein, fiber, and B vitamins in very few calories, which makes it a favorite in vegan and plant-based kitchens.
